notes: Refers only to someone who cooks as a profession, counted with 个 (gè) or 位 (wèi, polite). For someone who cooks at home, say 做饭的人 (person who cooks).

senses.definition: A person whose job is to prepare and cook food in a restaurant or hotel.

draftBefore.emotion: professional and focused, taking pride in creating a perfect dish
notes: Use 厨师 for a professional chef who works in a restaurant. If you are talking about someone who cooks at home as a hobby or a family member, it is more natural to use 厨子 (which can be informal) or simply describe them by saying 做饭的人 (the person who cooks).

faults.why: Wrong vowel in 厨: chú is /ʈʂʰu˧˥/, not retroflex /ʈʂʰɻ̩˧˥/, and 师 is /ʂʅ˥/ or /ʂɻ̩˥/.

faults.quote: cooking at home as a hobby or a family member... use 厨子
faults.why: 厨子 also means a professional cook (old-fashioned/informal), not a family member cooking at home.
